preferences.title: Simulation
preferences.operators: Enter arithmetic in x. Use * for multiplication, / for division, and ^ for powers. Parentheses control the order of operations.
preferences.functions: Use pi or e for constants. Supported functions are abs, sqrt, cbrt, exp, log, sin, cos, tan, and atan.
preferences.example: For example, sin(x) - x/2. Newton uses f′(x), or differentiates f numerically when f′(x) is blank. Fixed-Point Iteration needs a map g(x).

solver.heading: Starting conditions
solver.empty: Step or run to fill the history.
solver.continuity: A sign change brackets a root when f is continuous on the interval.
solver.open: An initial guess near a root can help the method converge.
solver.fixedHint: Choose a map whose fixed points solve f(x) = 0.
solver.expressionHelp: Use * for multiplication and ^ for powers.
solver.moveStartDescription: Use the left and right arrow keys, or A and D, to move the focused graph handle.
solver.moveStartFineDescription: Hold Shift while moving the graph handle to take smaller steps.
solver.keyText: Edit expressions and starting values, then press Enter to apply. Tab moves between controls.
solver.syntaxError: Check the expression and use only the supported symbols.
solver.pending: Apply to use the edited values.
solver.invalidBracket: Use a < b with opposite signs or an endpoint root.
solver.undefined: A value is undefined or too large.
solver.zeroSlope: The slope is zero or unusable.
solver.inconsistent: The fixed point does not solve f(x) = 0.
solver.bisectionDescription: Halve the bracket and keep the half that contains a sign change.
solver.newtonDescription: Follow the tangent to the x-axis to find the next estimate.
solver.falsePositionDescription: Use the chord’s x-intercept and keep a sign-changing bracket.
solver.secantDescription: Draw a secant through the last two guesses and follow it to the x-axis.
solver.fixedPointDescription: Follow g(x) vertically and y = x horizontally to create the next guess.
solver.brentDescription: Try interpolation and fall back to bisection when it offers safer progress.
solver.a11yControls: Choose an example or edit its expressions and starting values. Use Step for a single iteration.
solver.a11yHint: Try several steps and read the estimates in the history.
solver.axesApplyHelp: Enter or Apply axes sets the graph bounds.
solver.autoAxesHint: Edit a bound to set a manual view.
solver.manualAxesHint: Manual view. Turn on Auto zoom to follow the iteration.
solver.cobwebSource: Start on y = x at xₙ ≈ {{from}}.
solver.tangentBuild: Follow the tangent to y = 0. xₙ₊₁ = {{from}} − ({{fy}})/({{slope}}) ≈ {{x}}.
solver.chordBuild: Follow the endpoint chord to y = 0 at x ≈ {{x}}.
solver.secantBuild: Follow the secant to y = 0 at x ≈ {{x}}.
solver.inverseBuild: Fit x as a quadratic in y. At y = 0, the fit gives x ≈ {{x}}.
solver.brentThird: The third sample is c ≈ {{third}}, f(c) ≈ {{ty}}.
solver.brentProgress: Reject {{candidate}} because it reduces the step too little.
solver.brentTolerance: The previous move was below tolerance. Use the midpoint.
solver.brentNonfinite: The interpolation gave no finite estimate. Use the midpoint.
solver.cobwebBuild: Go up or down to g(xₙ) ≈ {{x}}, then across to y = x.
solver.keptDecision: f({{x}}) ≈ {{fx}}. Keep [{{low}}, {{high}}] because the signs are opposite.
solver.openDecision: Use {{x}} as the next guess. Its residual is {{residual}}.
solver.exactDecision: f({{x}}) = 0. This estimate is a root.
solver.fixedExactDecision: At x = {{x}}, g(x) = x and f(x) = 0.
solver.readyDecision: Press Step to see the first construction.
solver.cycle: The estimates repeat in a cycle.
solver.derivativeMismatch: Check f′(x): it does not match the slope of f(x).
solver.derivativeNumeric: f′(x) is blank, so the slope of f(x) is computed numerically.
solver.derivativeBlank: Leave f′(x) blank to differentiate f(x) numerically.
